passage: Note from the Class 5 teacher. At recess three boys imitated Gargi's short prayer before lunch, folding their hands and gabbling. Harsha laughed along with them, loudly at first. Gargi closed the tiffin and walked away, and Harsha's laugh stopped, leaving a stiff smile. When one boy started the act again, Harsha said, "Let's go and play." Afterwards I spoke with Harsha privately. Harsha said, "Everybody was laughing, so I did. I felt bad when Gargi left." I did not scold. We talked about what Harsha could do next time, and I will keep an eye on how the group treats Gargi.

qa.q: How many boys imitated Gargi's prayer?
What was Harsha feeling when Gargi closed the tiffin and walked away?
qa.a: Regret: Harsha's laugh stopped, and later Harsha said they joined in because everybody was laughing and felt bad when Gargi left.

qa.q: What braver choice could Harsha make next time?
qa.a: Stand quietly aside or change the subject, as Harsha began to do by saying, "Let's go and play."

qa.q: How might Gargi have felt during the imitation?
qa.a: Hurt and embarrassed, which is probably why Gargi closed the tiffin and walked away.

grounding: Illustrates a child laughing at a classmate's prayer to fit in, feeling bad, and starting to change the subject.
